what: Loads configs/models/<name>.yml on top of base.yml. Any key that file sets cannot also be set on the command line with a different value unless override_model_config=true (measured error on the Reading tab).

Which decoder layer class the decoder stacks: one of 25 DecoderBlockType values (llama2, gemma3, deepseek, qwen3, gpt3, ...). The running example is the gpt3 block: LayerNorm with bias, biased projections, learned positions.
Residual width d_model (multiplied by global_parameter_scale, 1 by default, to give emb_dim).
Number of query heads.
Number of key/value heads; fewer than query heads gives grouped-query attention. The gpt3 block asserts they are equal.
Hidden width of the MLP (per expert for MoE models use base_moe_mlp_dim).
Number of decoder layers; with scan_layers they are stacked into one array per weight.
Width of each attention head; MaxText sets it explicitly rather than deriving emb_dim / heads.
Activation per MLP input projection: ['silu','linear'] is SwiGLU (two input matrices, one gated); ['gelu'] is one matrix with jax.nn.gelu, which defaults to the tanh approximation.
Vocabulary size. It must divide by the mesh axes that shard it (the vocab rule maps to tensor axes): the running example's 65 cannot be split 4 ways.
Epsilon of RMSNorm or LayerNorm; 1e-5 here, PyTorch's LayerNorm default too.
Tie the output head to the token embedding (true) or keep a separate logits_dense kernel (false).
A positive value adds learned absolute position embeddings of that length (GPT-3 style); -1 means none (RoPE models).
One projection producing q, k and v together (a [embed, 3, heads, head_dim] kernel) instead of three.
Experts per MoE layer; 1 means a dense model.
Top-k routing: experts each token is sent to.
Expert capacity for token dropping; -1 (default) means dropless, with ragged all-to-all and grouped matmul instead of padding.
Activation and matmul dtype: bfloat16 by default.
Dtype of the stored parameters (and so of the optimizer's master copy): float32 by default.
Dtype gradients are cast to after value_and_grad, before clipping and the update.
Passed to the dots: default, high or highest. On TPU 'default' runs float32 matmuls in bfloat16 passes; on CPU it changes nothing (the runs here set highest for exact comparisons).
Cast the logits to float32 before the loss.
'' for none, or int8, fp8 variants and others through AQT or Qwix.
Run the decoder layers with jax.lax.scan over weights stacked on a 'layers' axis: compile time and HLO size stop growing with depth (measured on the Reading tab).
Which axis of each stacked weight is the layer axis: 1, so a [embed, mlp] kernel becomes [embed, layers, mlp]. The scan moves it to axis 0 at run time.

What the backward pass may keep from the forward pass of each layer (jax.checkpoint policy): 'full' keeps only the layer input and recomputes everything else; 'minimal' keeps the projections' outputs.
Keep optimizer state in host memory and move it to the device for the update.
Accumulate gradients over this many microbatches before one optimizer update.
Compute logits and loss in this many tiles to bound peak memory for large vocabularies.
Kernel: autoselected, dot_product, flash (splash attention in Pallas on TPU), cudnn_flash_te on GPU. 'autoselected' falls back to dot_product on CPU, for short sequences (under 128) and in decode.
Variant: global (causal), local_sliding, chunk, mla, full, compressed, block_diffusion.
Window for local_sliding attention.
Splash attention query block size (TPU kernel tiling); 512 by default.
auto: annotations plus GSPMD/Shardy propagation; explicit: sharding in the types (see Sharding and scale).

Ordered (logical name, mesh axes) pairs; each array dimension takes the first rule whose mesh axes are still free. A model file's rule replaces every base rule with the same name (llama2-7b.yml sets ['norm', 'fsdp'], so its norm scales are FSDP-sharded instead of split over 'tensor').
FSDP degree inside a slice (over ICI). -1 absorbs every device not used by other axes: on 8 devices with nothing else set, fsdp = 8.
Pure data parallelism inside a slice (replicated parameters).
Tensor parallelism inside a slice: heads, mlp and vocab dimensions split over 'tensor'.
Expert parallelism inside a slice.
Pipeline stages inside a slice (the 'stage' mesh axis).
Context (sequence) parallelism inside a slice.
Data parallelism across slices over the data-centre network; -1 absorbs the slices.
Number of TPU slices; -1 lets MaxText count them.
all_gather (default), ring, ulysses or usp.
Microbatches per pipeline step; the bubble is (stages - 1) / (repeats x microbatches + stages - 1) (base.yml:450).
Largest fraction of parameter bytes allowed to stay unsharded before MaxText raises.
Sequences per device per step; global batch = this x number of devices (12 x 8 = 96 on the 8 simulated devices here). Fractions below 1 are allowed.
Sequence length.
Training steps; also the default length of the learning-rate schedule.
Peak learning rate (3e-5 by default, a fine-tuning value).
cosine or wsd (warmup, stable, decay).
Fraction of the schedule spent in linear warmup, which starts at learning rate 0 at step 0.
Final learning rate as a fraction of the peak (1.0 makes the cosine flat, used here to match the running example).
adamw, adam_pax, sgd or muon.
Adam first-moment decay.
Adam second-moment decay: 0.95, the Llama 2 value (optax and PyTorch default to 0.999).
Adam epsilon, added outside the square root.
Decoupled weight decay coefficient.
Regexes of parameter paths NOT to decay. Empty by default, so biases, norm scales and embeddings are decayed too; the run here passed ['bias', 'scale', 'embedding'].
Global-norm clipping threshold; 0 disables it.
Dropout switch; with it off the run is a deterministic function of the seeds.
Dropout probability (0.0 by default, so dropout does nothing even when enabled).
Weight of the z-loss on the log-partition function (0 by default).
synthetic (default), hf, grain or tfds.
Pack several documents per sequence with segment ids so attention does not cross them.
sentencepiece, tiktoken or huggingface.
Shuffle the data source.
Seed for parameter initialisation.
Create the Orbax checkpointer. If the run directory already holds a checkpoint, training resumes from it.
Write checkpoints in the background while training continues.
Save every this many steps (10,000 by default).
Start from parameters only (no optimizer state), for fine-tuning.
Start from a full state: parameters, optimizer state and step.
How many checkpoints Orbax keeps, through its keep-latest-N preservation policy (common/checkpoint_context.py). The default None was not tested here.
tpu, gpu, gpu_multiprocess or cpu. MaxText's own CPU tests pass cpu, as the runs here do.
Names the output directory; reusing a name resumes that run.
Where checkpoints, metrics and logs go (a gs:// bucket in production; a local path here).
'' , xplane (the JAX profiler) or nsys.
Compile ahead of time for a named TPU topology (for example v5e-256) with train_compile.py; needs libtpu, so not run here.
Persistent compilation cache directory.
How often metrics are flushed.
